processMaps.name: Authentication & Access
processMaps.description: Every request's entry point: an LBA signs up, logs in to get a JWT, and that JWT is checked on every subsequent call before any domain Lambda runs.

1.title: Account Creation
1.description: A new LBA organisation signs up through the React frontend. AuthService hashes the password with bcrypt and creates the lbas and users rows, exactly as auth.py does today.

2.title: Login & Token Issuance
2.description: AuthService verifies the password hash and, instead of setting a session cookie, signs a JWT (user_id/lba_id/org_name/user_name/role claims — the same shape the cookie carried) using the secret in LBA-Prod-Security-JwtSigningKey, and returns it in the JSON response body.

3.title: Token Storage & Reuse
3.description: The React app holds the JWT in memory and sends it as Authorization: Bearer on every subsequent API call — no cookie, no SameSite/CORS cookie complications across the frontend/backend domain split.

4.title: Per-Request Authorization
4.description: Every protected route passes through LBA-Prod-Security-JwtAuthorizer first. It verifies the signature and expiry, then attaches lba_id/role/user_id to the request context so the domain Lambda can scope its query without re-deriving identity.

5.title: Logout
5.description: Logout is stateless — the frontend simply discards the in-memory token. AuthService's /auth/logout exists mainly for parity/audit logging, since there's no server-side session to invalidate.

processMaps.name: Farmer Register Onboarding
processMaps.description: An LBA uploads its real master farmer list (as big as the 1,938-row JIMGAF file) and the register becomes the source of truth every lot allocation checks against.

1.title: Template Retrieval
1.description: The LBA downloads the upload template — a presigned GET URL against the static templates bucket, not a file streamed through Lambda.

2.title: Bulk Upload & Parsing
2.description: The filled-in .xlsx is POSTed to FarmerRegisterService, which parses it with openpyxl using the same HEADER_ALIASES/_norm_header matching the current app validates against, then upserts every row into farmers, scoped to lba_id.

3.title: Register Browsing
3.description: GET /farmers (list/search) and GET /farmers/{code} (detail, with incentive history) read back what was uploaded, scoped to the authenticated tenant.

4.title: Per-Farmer Maintenance
4.description: Incentive records and active/inactive status are managed per farmer as before; these writes happen directly against farmers/incentives.

5.title: Export & Reset
5.description: GET /farmers/export generates a fresh .xlsx into the exports bucket and hands back a presigned URL. POST /farmers/clear-all remains the one destructive, confirmation-gated action, carried over unchanged.

processMaps.name: Lot Creation & Traceability
processMaps.description: A broker-sourced lot arrives with only a total weight and a receipt range. The system generates a plausible, quota-respecting farmer list for it automatically — the core value proposition of this app, unchanged by this migration.

1.title: Eligibility Check
1.description: Before showing the 'new lot' form, the frontend calls GET /lots/eligibility to know how many farmers currently have remaining quota — the same n_eligible count app.py computes today.

2.title: Lot Creation & Allocation
2.description: POST /lots runs allocation.py's proportional-split algorithm unchanged: validates the lot date isn't in the future, allocates volume across eligible farmers, derives each farmer's bag count from their own weight (max(1, round(vol/62.5)) — never 0), and gives each farmer receipt its own randomized delivered_date no later than the lot's own date.

3.title: Review Gate
3.description: The lot starts in 'pending' status, blocking quota but not yet counting as delivered. POST /lots/{id}/accept or /reject (admin/LBA role only) finalizes it, exactly as the current approval workflow does.

4.title: Delivery Slip Export
4.description: GET /lots/{id}/export regenerates the per-farmer delivery slip .xlsx into the exports bucket and returns a presigned URL — same per-farmer columns (receipt no., farmer, community, date delivered, bags, volume) as lot_result.html renders today.

processMaps.name: Platform Administration & Operations
processMaps.description: The cross-cutting admin surface (staff accounts, per-tenant settings, dashboard) plus how the whole stack is monitored, none of which changes the business logic — just where it runs.

1.title: Dashboard
1.description: GET /dashboard runs the same read-only aggregation across farmers/lots/lot_allocations that the landing page shows today.

2.title: Staff Account Management
2.description: Admin-only GET/POST /users and POST /users/{id}/toggle-active, with the admin check re-verified server-side from JWT claims rather than trusted from the frontend route guard alone.

3.title: Tenant Settings
3.description: GET/PUT /settings reads and writes the per-tenant settings table unchanged.

4.title: Operational Monitoring
4.description: Every Lambda writes to its own CloudWatch log group; an alarm on the aggregate error rate notifies the ops SNS topic so a bad deploy or a Lambda misbehaving in the existing VPC gets caught quickly.
